recent_articles.title: Bengal CID Serves Summons To Abhishek Banerjee In 'Fake Signature' Probe
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **West Bengal CID** served a notice to **Abhishek Banerjee**, TMC national general secretary, requesting his presence for questioning in a probe into alleged forged signatures on a letter supporting **Shobhandeb Chattopadhyay** as the Leader of Opposition. The notice was delivered after officers waited at Banerjee's residence and were directed to his alternative residence before finally serving him the summons.  The CID is investigating discrepancies in the signatures on a May 19 letter submitted by the TMC to the Assembly Secretariat, which some MLAs signed endorsing Chattopadhyay as the LoP. The probe has also questioned several TMC MLAs, including Nayna Banerjee and Kunal Ghosh.

recent_articles.title: CUET-UG exam hit by technical glitch; NTA orders probe, announces retest for 3765 candidates
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Hundreds** of candidates taking the **Common University Entrance Test Undergraduate (CUET-UG) 2026** in India faced disruption on Saturday due to a technical glitch at several examination centres. The **National Testing Agency (NTA)** ordered an investigation into the issue and announced a special re-examination for affected students. Nearly 95% of candidates completed their exams after services were restored, but 3,765 chose to leave before the test resumed.  The NTA will reschedule the exam for these candidates through a one-time special examination with details to be announced on the official CUET website.

recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Jammu and Kashmir** government announced it will file a review petition in the Supreme Court regarding the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) issue. recent_articles.title: School academic calendar nearly finalised - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A **Quality Improvement Programme (QIP)** monitoring committee met online on Saturday to finalize the academic calendar for the 2026-27 academic year. The proposed calendar includes 800 instructional hours for lower primary classes, 1,000 hours for upper primary with three additional Saturdays as working days, and 1,200 hours for high school with seven additional Saturdays.
